title: Der letzte Zug
desc: Everybody at the table knows their own
setting: Quarter past midnight in a pub, one story unfinished, and four different departure times.

options.feedback: Let him go. He said it in the middle of a sentence because that is how you catch a train without running.
His train is at twelve thirty-two and there is not another one. Asking is putting him in a corner.

options.es: Und der Rest von der Geschichte?
options.en: And the rest of the story?
options.feedback: You will get it next time. Everybody here has an unfinished story with somebody.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.en: And you? When does yours go?

options.es: Zwanzig nach. Ich habe noch Zeit.
options.en: Twenty past. I still have time.
options.feedback: Everybody has a number and everybody says it without checking. Yours is the twenty past bus.
Then you will be running at eighteen past, and running is the part people notice.
Eighty francs to Stans, less from here. Nobody does it, and saying so makes the table go quiet.
That is how it works and it is not meanness. Paying for somebody else needs a reason.
He will ask why, and he will really be asking. There is nothing wrong with it and it needs a reason.
There is no later. Pay at quarter past and you leave at ten past without a jacket in one hand.
Say it to each person, by name if you can. It takes thirty seconds and it is why you leave at ten past.
Understood everywhere and it is the German one. Ade is what this table says.

options.en: See you tomorrow at the office.
options.feedback: Warm, specific, and it names the next time. That is the whole move.
